items.title: Mission: Impossible - Fallout
items.reason: Practical stunt work at the top of the form, sustained across the whole runtime, with a real espionage plot holding it together.

items.title: Mad Max: Fury Road
items.reason: Essentially one continuous vehicular chase, at the highest intensity the genre offers.

items.title: Tenet
items.reason: A genuinely load-bearing high concept driving heists, chases and a reversed-time siege.

items.title: Fallout
items.reason: Wasteland action with a strong sci-fi premise, varied environments and a real mystery running underneath.

items.title: Hardcore Henry
items.reason: First-person action that almost never stops, built entirely around stunt work.

items.title: The Bourne Ultimatum
items.reason: Relentless pursuit structure - chases, close-quarters fights and a conspiracy that keeps escalating.

items.title: Kingsman: The Secret Service
items.reason: Wildly varied spy action with a strong comic streak and standout set pieces.

items.title: Extraction 2
items.reason: An extended single-take siege sequence anchors a film built to keep moving.

items.title: Gangs of London
items.reason: Brutally intense London crime warfare with sustained, varied violence and shifting factions.

items.title: The Raid 2
items.reason: Sprawling gangland sequel with prison riots, car combat and extraordinary close-quarters fighting.

items.title: Boss Level
items.reason: A time-loop premise used as an action engine: the same day, fought differently every time.

items.title: Reacher
items.reason: An overwhelmingly capable lead working through a small-town conspiracy, with regular decisive violence.

items.title: Extraction
items.reason: A mercenary extraction that becomes one long running battle across a city.

items.title: Crank
items.reason: A absurd chemical premise that forces its protagonist to keep moving and fighting for the entire runtime.

items.title: The Villainess
items.reason: Assassin revenge told through inventive first-person and vehicular fight staging.

items.title: The Old Guard
items.reason: Immortal mercenaries, close-quarters combat and gunplay, with a real hook behind the fighting.

items.title: Upgrade
items.reason: A cyberpunk implant premise that turns its lead into a passenger in his own body during fights.

items.title: The Night Agent
items.reason: Conspiracy and mole-hunting inside the White House, with regular pursuit and violence.

items.title: The Bourne Identity
items.reason: Amnesia, a hidden programme and the chase structure that defined the modern spy thriller.

items.title: Nobody
items.reason: A suburban nobody turns out to be extremely capable, and the film escalates steadily into sustained combat.

items.title: Bullet Train
items.reason: Competing assassins locked on one train, with constantly varied fights and absurd humour.

items.title: Banshee
items.reason: An ex-con impersonating a sheriff, with startlingly brutal fights breaking out through every episode.

items.title: The Night Comes for Us
items.reason: Close-quarters violence at extreme intensity, sustained for almost the entire runtime.

items.title: Edge of Tomorrow
items.reason: A time-loop premise applied to combat: die, learn, fight better, repeat.

items.title: Tom Clancy's Jack Ryan
items.reason: CIA analyst pulled into the field - conspiracy, moles and investigation with real action attached.

items.title: Into the Badlands
items.reason: Post-apocalyptic feudal territory war fought almost entirely with martial arts.

items.title: Altered Carbon
items.reason: Sleeve-swapping sci-fi noir: a murder mystery, a strong premise and regular violence.

items.title: Atomic Blonde
items.reason: Cold War Berlin spycraft with a stairwell fight that reset expectations for the genre.

items.title: Shoot 'Em Up
items.reason: A cartoon-logic gunfight premise sustained, without apology, from the first minute to the last.

items.title: Deadpool
items.reason: Fourth-wall-breaking revenge with sustained, inventive violence and a genuinely transgressive comic register.
